fix_commit_message:
Fix a bug in the NOT NULL/IS NULL optimization of check-in [cb94350185f555c3] that can cause invalid data to be used for a column if that column has a CHECK constraint that includes the NOT NULL or IS NULL operator. Problem discovered by the [https://issues.chromium.org/issues/415397143|Chromium fuzzer].  Never seen in the wild, as far as anybody knows.

FossilOrigin-Name: 2adaee9aa90f280a406007695fbc4a314806584c93d6b62b46c031492b31ec27
agent_reasoning: Without this guard, sqlite3VdbeTypeofColumn() is called unconditionally on the register returned by sqlite3ExprCodeTemp() in the TK_ISNULL/TK_NOTNULL codegen paths of sqlite3ExprIfTrue()/sqlite3ExprIfFalse(). When that register is a shared column-cache register (regFree1==0) rather than a fresh temp, tagging the preceding OP_Column with OPFLAG_TYPEOFARG permanently taints the cached register: on a later use of the same column (e.g. a CHECK constraint referencing the same NOT NULL/IS NULL column), OP_Column returns a pointer into the small fixed-size sqlite3CtypeMap[] array paired with the column's true (possibly huge) byte length instead of real data. A subsequent instruction like OP_MakeRecord then memcpy's using that bogus length, causing an out-of-bounds read past the 256-byte array and writing invalid data into the new record. Guarding the tagging with `if( regFree1 )` ensures only genuinely disposable temporaries are ever marked typeof-only, eliminating the unsound reuse; the added assert in OP_MakeRecord is a defensive backstop that would trip in debug builds if the sentinel pointer were ever copied as real data.
